title: repository.bootstrap creates the repository, commits the scaffold and binds it
description:
SPIDR child 2 of task-5ef1a0a9010c4bfe872ff9b774068234 (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05). dependsOn child 1 task-4a0f706437a042059789be2ebdb98bc0 for the scaffold it writes.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: the operator-only `repository.bootstrap` command and everything it does on disk - `git init`, write child 1's scaffold, first commit 'chore: scaffold by Moe', OPTIONAL `gh repo create <owner>/<name> --<visibility> --source . --push`, then bind it as the project repository via the EXISTING `project.bind_repository` and register it in the manager catalog - plus the `moe-bootstrap-receipt/1` receipt. No UI - child 3.

GITHUB IS OPTIONAL AND THAT IS LOAD-BEARING. A local-only bootstrap SUCCEEDS and SAYS SO. `gh` absent refuses BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE for the GitHub half while the local repository still exists, is committed and is bound - the receipt records remoteUrl: null. Getting this backwards (failing the whole bootstrap because `gh` is missing) would make the feature unusable on any machine without the GitHub CLI, which is most of them.

REUSE, DO NOT REINVENT: `project.bind_repository` already binds an existing repository and is what this row calls once the directory is a repository - do not write a second binding path. The `gh` invocation follows the same discipline chosen for Gate 3 (task-f961dc899a13488da8f119abdc37631f): the CLI on the operator's machine, refusing cleanly when absent, never a stored token.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04): `grep -rc 'repo create' apps/ tools/` = 0; no GitHub repository creation path exists. `moe init` scaffolds a store, not a product.

FOUR REFUSALS, and the directory one is the safety property: BOOTSTRAP_DIR_NOT_EMPTY (never write into a directory with contents - this command writes a whole tree and a wrong path could bury someone's work), BOOTSTRAP_GIT_UNAVAILABLE, BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE (partial, as above), BOOTSTRAP_PROFILE_VERSION_UNKNOWN (defined by child 1, raised here).
definitionOfDone: `repository.bootstrap` published OPERATOR-ONLY and MCP-EXCLUDED, in HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS, with the full roster backfill and a bidirectional set-equality roster test enumerating the served kinds from the dispatch seam; verify by deleting the entry from each side in turn and confirming both go red.

BOOTSTRAP_DIR_NOT_EMPTY is asserted with code AND layer against a directory containing ONE file, and the test asserts NOTHING was written - this command writes a whole tree, and a wrong path that buries an existing directory is the worst outcome in this row. Also assert a non-existent directory is created, and an EMPTY existing one is accepted.

A local-only bootstrap SUCCEEDS with `gh` absent: the directory is a git repository, `git log --oneline` is exactly ONE line ('chore: scaffold by Moe'), the repository is bound through the EXISTING `project.bind_repository`, the project is in the manager catalog, and the receipt records BOOTSTRAPPED with remoteUrl: null and the code BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE for the GitHub half. Assert all of it - a bootstrap that fails wholesale without `gh` is unusable on most machines.

GitHub creation is tested OFFLINE through an injectable port asserting the `gh` ARGV byte-for-byte (`gh repo create <owner>/<name> --<visibility> --source . --push`); BOOTSTRAP_GIT_UNAVAILABLE and BOOTSTRAP_PROFILE_VERSION_UNKNOWN each assert code + layer.

`moe-bootstrap-receipt/1` records {dir, sha, remoteUrl|null, BOOTSTRAPPED|REFUSED(code)}, mirroring repository/landing-receipt-contracts.ts; read it back from a real store and assert every member, including that a REFUSED receipt carries its code and no sha.
Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` (packages/contracts and the generated client are touched by the new kind).
taskRails: NEVER WRITE INTO A NON-EMPTY DIRECTORY. BOOTSTRAP_DIR_NOT_EMPTY is a safety property, not a validation nicety: this command writes a whole tree and the operator supplies the path.
A LOCAL-ONLY BOOTSTRAP IS A SUCCESS. `gh` absent refuses only the GitHub half; the repository still exists, is committed and is bound, and the receipt says remoteUrl: null.
REUSE `project.bind_repository` for the binding and child 1's generator for the tree. A second binding path or an inline scaffold defeats both rows.
`gh` CLI ONLY, matching the Gate 3 decision (task-f961dc89): no stored token, no REST fallback.
NEVER HAND-EDIT the generated client: run the generator and quote the OLD and NEW GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST.

implementationPlan.description:

Run and record the output of all three:
- `git grep -n "repository.bootstrap" -- packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts` — must hit (child task-c2b5a9f09c684569ae13b60b09128f82).
- `git grep -rn "BOOTSTRAP_DIR_NOT_EMPTY" -- apps/daemon/src` — must hit the engine module (child task-28fb953b96874889974d5f2b2c434e4e).
- `git grep -rn "CONTROLLED_PROFILE_VERSION" -- apps/daemon/src` — must hit (task-4a0f706437a042059789be2ebdb98bc0).

If ANY is absent, STOP and `moe.report_blocked` with `blockedOnTaskIds` naming the missing rows. Do NOT re-implement the missing surface here and do NOT narrow the DoD — a second engine or a second contract entry is a silent duplicate that collides with its owner in the shared worktree.

Also re-measure, and record, the five hard counts this row will move: `grep -n "toHaveLength(47)\|size).toBe(47)\|toHaveLength(12)" apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.test.ts` and `grep -n "toHaveLength(11)" apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry-human-approver.test.ts`. Peers land rows continuously; the numbers in this plan were measured at plan time and may have moved.

VOCABULARY: the kind, operator-only, and the automatic MCP fence. Edit `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts` (386 lines at plan time — see the size guard below):

1. A `REPOSITORY_BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_KIND = "repository.bootstrap" as const` constant beside the existing kind constants.
2. Add it to the `WiredCommandKind` union.
3. Add it to the EXISTING `BOOTSTRAP_FAMILY` table with the same capability `project.bind_repository` demands (CAPABILITIES.ADMIN, vocabulary.ts:79). `BOOTSTRAP_FAMILY` is already in `FAMILY_TABLES` at :189 — do NOT create a new family table, and do NOT touch `FAMILY_TABLES`.
4. Add its `PAYLOAD_KEYS` entry, matching the payload child task-c2b5a9f09c684569ae13b60b09128f82 published in the shared contract (dir, productName, profileVersion, plus the optional owner/name/visibility). Read the contract entry and mirror it — do not invent a second shape.
5. Add it to `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS`.

STEP 5 IS THE MCP FENCE AND IT IS AUTOMATIC. `mcp-tool-allowlist.ts:78` derives `MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS` as `[...OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS].filter((kind) => !MCP_REACHABLE_OPERATOR_KINDS.has(kind))`, and its comment states the contract explicitly: a kind that becomes operator-only leaves the MCP roster with no edit there. So `mcp-tool-allowlist.ts` gets NO source edit — only its counts move, in step 5. Because the fence and the payload entry are in the SAME file and the same commit, there is no landed HEAD at which the kind is MCP-advertised.

SIZE GUARD: `wc -l apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts` after the edit. It was 386 and the hard cap is 400. If it crosses, move the `BOOTSTRAP_FAMILY` table into the EXISTING `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-families.ts` (which the vocabulary's own comment at :186 says already reads the same list) rather than adding a new module. Do not leave it over 400.

REGISTER THE HANDLER IN THE BOOTSTRAP FAMILY — not in the registry.

`apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.ts:194` already spreads `...BOOTSTRAP_HANDLERS`. That file is 449 lines and ALREADY past the 400 hard cap before this row starts: add nothing to it.

1. `apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-contracts.ts` — add `"repository.bootstrap"` to the bootstrap command-kind list at :38 alongside `"project.bind_repository"`.
2. `apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-sequence.ts` — declare its prerequisites. `project.bind_repository` requires `project.register` first (:36); `repository.bootstrap` must land in the same ordering and the sequence's switch at :106 must handle it. State the chosen ordering in the step note.
3. `apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-services.ts` — add ONE entry to `BOOTSTRAP_HANDLERS` (:223) pointing at a thin adapter that: validates the payload, calls child task-28fb953b96874889974d5f2b2c434e4e's bootstrap service with the host ports, then on success routes the binding through the EXISTING `bindRepository` (:227) and registers the project in `apps/daemon/src/projects/project-catalog.ts`. The adapter is an ADAPTER — no git, no gh, no filesystem walk, no second binding path. If you find yourself writing process-spawn code here, it belongs in child A and you should stop and report.

DO NOT EDIT `apps/daemon/src/daemon-store-dependencies.test.ts`. Its assertion at :238 (`registry.keys()` set-equal to `Object.keys(PAYLOAD_KEYS)` minus `planning.submit_decomposition`) needs no change when this is done right — it is the tripwire that reds if step 2 added the payload key while this step did not register the handler. If it reds, the wiring is half-done; fix the wiring, never the assertion.

HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS. Add `"repository.bootstrap"` to the set at `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawn-contract.ts:195`, beside the existing `"repository.publish"` entry and under a comment in the same voice: creating a product repository at an operator-supplied path is the operator's decision; the wrapper performs it as an effect of that decision, never as staffed work.

This is a plain addition — no count guard and no membership guard reads `HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS`, unlike the MCP exclusion roster. Confirm that by grepping for a length assertion over it before assuming: `git grep -n "HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS" -- apps/daemon` (three source files at plan time: agent-spawn-contract.ts, agent-wrapper.ts, http/affordance-planning-offers.test.ts). If any of them asserts a size, that count moves in step 5 too.

ROSTER COUNT BACKFILL. Every one of these is invisible to a grep for the kind literal, which is exactly why they are enumerated here rather than left for discovery. Use the numbers you RE-MEASURED in step 1, not the plan-time ones, and move each by exactly one:

- `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.test.ts` — :862 `ROWS).toHaveLength(47)`, :863 `deps.registry.size).toBe(47)`, :870 `REGISTRATION_ORDER).toHaveLength(47)` -> 48; :1040 `OPERATOR_ONLY).toHaveLength(12)` -> 13. If `REGISTRATION_ORDER` or `ROWS` also transcribes the kinds by hand, insert the entry in the position the file's own ordering demands.
- `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry-human-approver.test.ts` — :325 `expectedExclusions).toHaveLength(11)` and :326 `MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS).toHaveLength(11)` -> 12. Both, and check whether `expectedExclusions` is a transcribed list that also needs the entry.
- `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts` — add or update whatever arms pin the family table, the payload keys and the operator-only set.

A count bumped without the corresponding roster entry, or an entry added without the count, is a half-done job that the step-3 weld will catch. Run `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` after this step and read the OUTPUT, not the exit code.

BIDIRECTIONAL ROSTER TEST (DoD 1). Add an arm to `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.test.ts`, next to the existing served-origin roster arm at :795-812 which is the pattern to follow.

The arm must assert SET EQUALITY, not a subset, between:
- the ADVERTISED set — the roster constant; and
- the SERVED set — enumerated from the IMPLEMENTATION SEAM (the dispatch port's handled kinds / the composed registry's keys), NOT from the roster constant.

Why the direction matters: a test that iterates the roster can only see one direction. Deleting an entry shrinks its own iteration and stays green while a served capability silently vanishes from the advertised surface. Enumerating the served side from the seam is what makes the second direction observable.

VERIFY BOTH DIRECTIONS BY MUTATION, and record both results in the step note: delete `repository.bootstrap` from the roster constant, confirm RED; restore. Delete it from the served side (the `BOOTSTRAP_HANDLERS` entry), confirm RED; restore. An arm that only reds one way has not been shown to hold. Prove each restore before moving on — these are TRACKED files, so `git diff -- <path>` is a valid restore proof here.

THE JOURNEY (DoD 2, 3, 4, 5) — one new test file, `apps/daemon/src/repository/repository-bootstrap-journey.test.ts`, exercising the REGISTERED command through the dispatch seam rather than calling the engine directly. Child A unit-proves these behaviours; this proves they survive the wiring.

Arms:
(a) DIRECTORY GUARD, the safety property: dispatch against a real temp directory containing exactly ONE file. Assert the refusal CODE `BOOTSTRAP_DIR_NOT_EMPTY` AND its layer — never merely that it failed. Then read the directory back and assert its entries are UNCHANGED: this command writes a whole tree, and proving nothing was written is the point of the arm. Also assert a non-existent directory IS created and an EMPTY existing one IS accepted.
(b) LOCAL-ONLY SUCCESS with the gh port reporting absent: the directory is a git repository; `git log --oneline` is EXACTLY ONE line reading `chore: scaffold by Moe` (assert the line count as well as the text); the repository is bound through the EXISTING `project.bind_repository` path (assert the bind event, not a re-implementation); the project is present in `apps/daemon/src/projects/project-catalog.ts`'s catalog; the result is BOOTSTRAPPED with remoteUrl: null AND carries `BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE` for the GitHub half. A bootstrap that fails wholesale without `gh` is unusable on most machines — this arm is what stops that regression.
(c) GITHUB ARGV, OFFLINE: through the injectable port, assert the captured `gh` argv BYTE-FOR-BYTE. No network in any arm.
(d) `BOOTSTRAP_GIT_UNAVAILABLE` and `BOOTSTRAP_PROFILE_VERSION_UNKNOWN` each assert CODE AND LAYER. For the profile-version code, note in the record that child 1 defines it and this row is the call site that raises it — that is the composition the DoD asks for, not a manufactured one.
(e) RECEIPT READ-BACK from a REAL store (not a fixture double): `moe-bootstrap-receipt/1` with every member — dir, sha, remoteUrl|null, BOOTSTRAPPED. And a REFUSED receipt carrying its code and NO sha.

TEARDOWN IS MANDATORY (epic rail 4): every temp directory and store handle is removed in a `finally`, not after the assertions — a throwing arm must not leak. A test that leaks a directory or a handle makes every later gate on this board inadmissible.

GATES (DoD 6). Run each leg standalone and quote its OUTPUT — the `Test Files N passed` count line — never its exit code. `pnpm --filter <pkg> <script>` prints "No projects matched the filters" and exits 0; "No test files found" also exits 0.

- `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` (@moe/daemon is apps/daemon — resolve by PACKAGE NAME).
- `pnpm typecheck`.
- `pnpm test` — the DoD names it because packages/contracts and the generated client are root-lane. State explicitly that the root include has NO `apps/**`, so this leg is NOT evidence for anything under apps/daemon; the daemon leg above is.
- `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` — run it and quote the count line. The epic rail requires it for any row touching the shared roster, and two contract-digest mirrors live under apps/control-room where `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck` and the daemon leg cannot see them. If child task-c2b5a9f09c684569ae13b60b09128f82 already moved the mirrors, say so and quote the leg anyway.

REPO-WIDE BASELINE, path-attributed: record repo-wide failures at the merge-base and at HEAD, subtract, intersect with this row's owned paths. Completion needs that intersection EMPTY and the owned legs exit 0. Disclose any foreign red verbatim with its failing file paths — never hide it, never fabricate a green.

PRE-EXISTING BREACH TO DISCLOSE, NOT FIX: `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.ts` is 449 lines, past the 400 cap, at the merge-base and untouched by this row. Record that measurement in the completion record so it is attributed correctly, and file it as a follow-up comment rather than a new row.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW. Read the diff as an attacker before `moe.complete_task`.

SECURITY-SHAPED QUESTIONS, answered with a command each:
- Is there any landed state in this commit at which `repository.bootstrap` is MCP-ADVERTISED? Compute `wiredMcpToolKinds()` at HEAD and assert the kind is absent. The MCP port authenticates with the operator bootstrap credential, so an advertised operator kind means an agent arrives AS THE OPERATOR.
- Is it actually operator-only? Dispatch it as a non-operator principal and assert the refusal code and layer.
- Is it in `HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS`, so no wrapper can staff it?
- Does the directory guard refuse BEFORE the first byte is written, or after? Point the command at a directory holding a file whose bytes you hash first, and assert the hash afterwards. This is the worst-outcome path in the row.
- Does the payload validate the operator-supplied `dir`? A path that escapes, a UNC path, an empty string, and a path that is a FILE rather than a directory each need a defined answer.

CORRECTNESS QUESTIONS:
- What happens if the command runs TWICE against the same directory? The second run must hit `BOOTSTRAP_DIR_NOT_EMPTY`, not append a second commit — assert it.
- What happens if `git init` succeeds and the commit fails? Is the receipt REFUSED with no sha, and is the directory left in a state a retry can describe? Say which, in the record.
- Does any error path put a token, a remote URL credential, or an operator path into a log line or a receipt? Epic rail 3: a secret never surfaces in plaintext, including on the error path.

MUTATION DRILL: `git status --porcelain` the exact paths first. The journey test file is NEW (untracked), so `git diff -- <path>` certifies NOTHING for it — back it up out of tree under %TEMP% suffixed by your worker id and prove the restore by SHA256 equality in a call SEPARATE from the restore. The vocabulary and roster files are TRACKED, so `git diff` is a valid restore proof for those.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
SPLITTING THIS ROW. Not optional -- measured, not felt. The DoD wants the kind published (13 edits), the engine (ports, git, gh, receipt), and the journey. Two children were filed before this plan:
- task-28fb953b96874889974d5f2b2c434e4e -- the bootstrap ENGINE leaf (dir guard, git init, scaffold write, first commit, gh port, `moe-bootstrap-receipt/1`), dependsOn the scaffold row task-4a0f7064.
- task-c2b5a9f09c684569ae13b60b09128f82 -- the SHARED-CONTRACT publication (RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS, the hand-transcribed roster at runtime-contract.test.ts:35, the regenerated client and the six GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST mirrors).
This row's dependsOn was set to all three via moe.set_task_dependencies (confirmed: previousDependsOn had one id, now three).

WHY THE CONTRACT HALF DETACHES. apps/daemon/src/goals/goal-create-with-source.ts:35 documents a kind that IS in RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS and NOT in the daemon table. The two rosters are deliberately not set-equal, so the intermediate HEAD is a landed documented state, not a hole.

WHY THE MCP FENCE AND THE REGISTRATION STAY IN ONE ROW. Registering a kind before fencing it advertises it over MCP, and the MCP port authenticates with the operator bootstrap credential -- an agent would arrive AS THE OPERATOR for the duration of a row. Here the fence is derived from OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS in the same file as PAYLOAD_KEYS, so both land in the same commit by construction and no advertisement window exists at any landed HEAD.

WHERE THE DoD's BEHAVIOURAL CLAUSES ARE PROVEN. Items 2-5 (dir guard, local-only success, gh argv, receipt) are unit-proven in child A and RE-PROVEN here end-to-end through the registered command in one journey test. That is stronger evidence than repeating the unit arms: it exercises the dispatch seam, the bind through the existing `project.bind_repository`, the catalog entry and the receipt read-back from a real store in one pass. It is not a narrowed DoD -- every clause is asserted, once through the real seam.
